newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan urges West to revise Iraq strategy.
newsitem.headline: Jordan urges West to revise Iraq strategy.

text.p: Jordan's Crown Prince Hassan urged the West on Saturday to re-think its policy towards Iraq after six years of crippling trade sanctions.

The prince said he welcomed the long-awaited agreement on implementing U.N. Security Council resolution 986, which allows Iraq to sell $2 billion of oil over six months to buy urgently needed food and medicine.

But he said Western powers should not allow the limited relief for Iraq's civilian population as a reason to maintain a hard line on Iraq, which has suffered stringent U.N. trade sanctions since its 1990 invasion of Kuwait.

"We do take pride in some good news -- 986 -- relaxation on the human condition in Iraq, but leading to what?" Prince Hassan told delegates to a Euro-Arab parliamentary dialogue in Jordan. "Leading to a new strategy, this is our hope."

Jordan's King Hussein turned against Iraqi President Saddam Hussein after years of close ties. But Jordanians still have strong ties with their neighbours and continue to trade with Iraq under an annual protocol covering humanitarian goods exempted from the sanctions.
